# Dōbutsu no Mori e+ PC/Android port v1.4.15

Version 1.4.15 of the port that runs [afe-decomp](https://github.com/cailet0422/afe-decomp) (the どうぶつの森 e+ decompilation) on PC and Android.

## Changes since v1.4.14

**The game keeps its speed where the screen cannot show 60 frames a second.** On some phones (reported on a Galaxy
A36) the picture looked smooth but the game went in slow motion: walking, running, the villagers, animations and
text all moved slower than they should.

The game takes one step per frame, 60 a second. Until now each frame simply waited until 1/60 s after the previous
one, and nothing made up for a frame that came late. Where drawing and showing a frame takes longer than 1/60 s (a
phone's GPU, more so with the HD texture pack, or VSync on a display that shows fewer frames), the game therefore ran
exactly as much slower as the screen was, at a steady frame rate that still looked smooth: at 40 frames a second the
game ran at two thirds of its speed.

Now the frames have fixed slots on a 60 Hz schedule. When frames come late, the next ones start at once, and when the
game is a whole frame behind, the next frame is played without being drawn or shown. Playing a frame without drawing
it costs very little (drawing is the slow part), so the game keeps its full speed and the screen shows fewer frames
instead:

- at most 2 frames in a row are not shown, so at least every third frame is;
- a frame that copies the screen (the scene behind a menu, a photo) is always drawn;
- after a pause for loading or saving, or with the app in the background, the game does not rush through what it
  missed;
- where the phone's processor itself is too slow (a frame not drawn still takes most of a frame's time), all frames are
  shown as before, as skipping would only make the picture choppy;
- the PC versions get the same, with the frame limiter on (F3 turns it off and on as before). The window title now
  counts the frames shown.

On Android, `log.txt` (in the app's folder) gets a line once a minute while frames are being left out, e.g.
`[VI] 60 s: 3600 game frames (100% of full speed), 2250 shown (37.5 a second); ...`, which tells how many frames the
device shows.

- Signed with the same key as the previous version, so it installs over it (saves, the Korean patch and texture
  packs are kept).

## Updating

- **From v1.0.0 or later**, the game finds this version when it starts and offers to update (**Update now**; on
  Android, **업데이트** in the dialog). If GitHub answers with an error, try again a little later.
- v0.1.6 and earlier cannot update themselves: install this version by hand once.
- The multiplayer protocol is the same as v1.4.x's: v1.4.0 to v1.4.15 can be in the same room, and 32-bit and
  64-bit players can play together.

## Read this first

- **No game data is included.** You need your own disc image of the Japanese 「どうぶつの森 e+」 **Rev 1 (GAEJ01)**
  (`.iso` / `.ciso` / `.gcm`) to run it. Disc images are not distributed.
- **To play in Korean**, download the Korean patch from [retrodb 한글패치 — 동물의 숲 e+](https://retrodb.info/krpatch/7428/%EB%8F%99%EB%AC%BC%EC%9D%98-%EC%88%B2-e)
  and apply it in the game (pause menu → Settings → Disc → Korean patch → Install...). The Korean patch is the work of an
  independent author (역전맞고) unrelated to this repository.
- Multiplayer: [README](https://github.com/cailet0422/afe-port/blob/main/README.md#multiplayer). For players from
  other networks, the surest way is UPnP turned on in the host's router, or UDP 47070 forwarded to the host's device.

## Files

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `DobutsuNoMoriEPlus-v1.4.15-Windows-x64.zip` | 64-bit Windows. Includes `SDL2.dll`, requires OpenGL 3.3 |
| `DobutsuNoMoriEPlus-v1.4.15-Windows-x86.zip` | 32-bit Windows (also runs on 64-bit Windows). Includes `SDL2.dll`, requires OpenGL 3.3 |
| `DobutsuNoMoriEPlus-v1.4.15-Linux-x86_64.zip` | 64-bit Linux. Requires SDL2 (`libsdl2-2.0-0`) and an OpenGL 3.3 driver |
| `DobutsuNoMoriEPlus-v1.4.15-Android.apk` | Android 5.0 or later, 32/64-bit ARM (armeabi-v7a, arm64-v8a) |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | SHA-256 of the files above |

## Verified

Measured in the test container, whose software renderer (llvmpipe) draws only 30 to 40 frames a second, the same
situation as a phone that cannot show 60. The game's speed is the game frames played per second of real time:

| | v1.4.14 | v1.4.15 |
|---|---|---|
| Title demo, same frames every run (`--deterministic`), 80 s of game time | 141 s, **57%** of full speed | 80.2 s, **99.8%**, 27–48 frames shown a second |
| Title demo as played (random town), without HD textures | 41.8 frames a second, **70%** | **100%**, 37 frames shown a second |
| Same as the first row with the HD texture pack (ACHD v25, decoded at half size as on most phones) | 163 s, **49%** | 80.9 s, **98.9%** |
| Title demo as played with the HD texture pack, two runs | 27 frames a second, **45%** | **100%** and **70%** (the heaviest scenes, where one frame takes over 50 ms here) |

- The game plays the same frames whether they are shown or not: with `--deterministic`, all screenshots and the whole
  audio dump of v1.4.15, which left about 40% of the frames unshown, are byte for byte those of v1.4.14 (title demo,
  with and without the HD pack). The town map opened over the town on frames that were to be skipped shows the town
  behind it, the same as v1.4.14.
- `--sim-refresh 20` (a new test option that imitates a VSync display of 20 Hz) keeps 97–100% of the speed with 20
  frames shown a second.
- The 43 scripted scenarios run for every release give the same 921 screenshots, logged positions and saves on
  v1.4.14 and on this version.
- Four of them (a tour of the town, all the buildings, the town in late autumn, an NES game) were also played with
  every frame drawn, as on a 40 Hz VSync display (`--sim-refresh 40`), in a container busy enough that 17–26% of the
  frames were not shown. The positions are the same as without skipping, and so are the 128 screenshots but two:
  those of a menu, where the fast test mode leaves the scene behind it black and these runs show the room.
- With the frame limiter off (F3), nothing changes. All unit tests pass.
- Android: the release-key signature (certificate `db6fc1ad…`) and the version (1.4.15, versionCode 10415).

## Known limitations

- No test on a real phone was possible here; the slow screen was reproduced with the container's software renderer.
- Where one frame takes more than about 50 ms to draw (under 20 frames a second), the game still falls behind: at most
  2 frames in a row are left out.
- The limitations of v1.4.3 remain (see its [release notes](https://github.com/cailet0422/afe-port/releases/tag/v1.4.3)).

Build instructions and detailed progress are in [docs/README.md](https://github.com/cailet0422/afe-port/blob/main/docs/README.md).
